title: Thirty billion on the desk
summary: Meta's Muse Glimmer puts a thirty-billion-parameter multimodal agent model into a testable local memory envelope using quantization, cache-efficient attention, and a bundled speculative drafter. Recursive Synthetic Terminal Tasks grows verified terminal work across fifteen generations, while an internal score conflict and the gap between solvability and usefulness keep its strongest claim in check.

dives.story: Muse Glimmer's local multimodal agent design
dives.why_it_matters: Teams handling private documents, local code, or intermittent connectivity can now test a permissively licensed agent model sized for one well-equipped machine, but they need workload evidence on memory, tool accuracy, and data that leaves through connected services.

Coding-agent and post-training teams need cheaper executable tasks whose instructions, environments, solutions, and verifiers stay aligned as difficulty grows, without confusing generated solvability with representative real-world work.

concepts_taught: solution-first recursive terminal-task synthesis: extending an executable reference path, realigning the environment, public instruction, and private verifier, enforcing oracle and contract validity, then reseeding accepted tasks
